key_insight: Explicit evidence-grounding constraints improved clinical alignment in LLM-generated menstrual health summaries, but made them harder to read.
clinical_relevance: Patient-facing health summaries need to preserve clinical meaning and uncertainty while remaining understandable.
method: Generated menstrual health narratives from structured records using a prompt-based constrained framework.
Combined structured evidence conditioning with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
Evaluated alignment with natural language inference, atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures.
evidence_signal: Across three LLMs and 4,500 summaries, grounding improved uncertainty preservation and generally maintained or improved faithfulness when evaluated against retrieved evidence; omission effects varied by model.
watch_item: Greater alignment came with harder reading and more medical terminology; the abstract does not establish patient comprehension or clinical benefit.
paper_title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
